messages:
Maria N.: quick RFC follow-up: sketched a dynamic probe-budget allocator for kernel selection. TL;DR: allocate probe budget by tail-latency risk + model-seqlen entropy, not flat samples.
Ajay K.: can you paste the allocator formula? curious how we weight tail vs entropy.
Maria N.: sure — conceptually: budget = base + alpha * tail_risk + beta * seq_entropy. tail_risk = pct95_latency_delta / pct95_baseline. seq_entropy estimated from recent seq-len histogram. alpha/beta tuned per tier.
Liam P.: how do we measure seq_entropy in practice? sliding window? per-tenant or global?
Maria N.: per-route sliding window (5min) with exponential decay. we bucket seq lengths coarsely (16,32,64,128,256,512,>512) to keep memory small.
Eve S.: what about cold-models or new ver rollouts? need min probes otherwise fallback chooses slow kernel.
Maria N.: agreed. we enforce a min_probe_count of 20 for new model-variant IDs for first 30min, then allocator takes over.
Devon R.: i worry about probe noise — probing itself can perturb hot paths. any backoff?
Maria N.: yes: probes are prioritized in low-util backfill slots and we apply probe_backoff_factor on high p50 CPU/GPU utl. default backoff=0.5 (halves budget when host > 80% util).
Ajay K.: can we see a sample probe invocation? a short command that infra can run.
Maria N.: posted example:
```bash
# run quick probe for LLama-70b candidate kernel
probe-kernel --model "llama-70b" --variant q8 --seqlen 512 --samples 50 --concurrency 4 --output /tmp/probe-70b-q8.json
``` 
Liam P.: output format ok? need pct50/pct95/pct99 + mem/gpu-util + sample-seqlen-dist.
Maria N.: yes, schema: {"kernel":...,"latency":{"p50":..,"p95":..,"p99":..},"gpu_mem_mb":..,"seq_hist":{...}}
runtime-bot: probe finished: llama-70b q8 on node g4-12, p50=32ms, p95=120ms, p99=320ms, mem=8423MB (results stored s3://redwood-probes/1837123456.json)
Eve S.: for caching decisions: do we let allocator prefer KV-cache-friendly kernels? e.g., ones with low warmup amplification?
Maria N.: good point — we add a warmup_penalty term to score = latency + gamma*warmup_amplification where warmup_amplification = extra_tokens_needed_to_reach steady throughput. gamma defaults to 0.8 for chat-heavy routes.
Devon R.: how to measure warmup_amplification cheaply? full prefill sims are expensive.
Maria N.: we use a micro-benchmark: repeated single-turn generation with cached vs uncached states to infer kv-fill slope. cheap ~100 samples per kernel.
Ajay K.: rollout policy — if allocator flips preferred kernel, how do we avoid oscillation?
Maria N.: hysteresis: require sustained improvement > threshold for window T (default 10min) and limit swaps to 1 per model variant per 15min. also add probe confidence interval — only act if p95 CI excludes current p95.
Liam P.: monitoring/alerts?
Maria N.: dashboard tile: probe success rate, budget consumption, swap count, and a small regression alert when chosen kernel's p95 increases >10% vs baseline. also log every swap as an audit event.
Eve S.: can we add an opt-out annotation on routes that must keep a fixed kernel? enterprise customers will ask.
Maria N.: added config: route.annotations.kernel.lock=true. allocator respects that.
Devon R.: what's next action? implement prototype and run against 3 canary models?
Maria N.: yep. action items: (1) Devon + Liam to implement probe runner shim (due EOD+3), (2) Ajay to add metric metadata + dashboard (EOD+5), (3) Eve to draft enterprise opt-out config + docs (EOD+4). I'll wire up the allocator config in the RFC text and push update.
Ajay K.: acked. I'll also add a small simu harness to validate hysteresis thresholds offline.
Liam P.: will start on shim. quick q: where to store probe results? S3 prefix?
Maria N.: use s3://redwood-probes/<date>/kernel/<thread_ts>-<model>-<variant>.json. runtime-bot will emit link.
runtime-bot: noted and will upload when probes run.
Maria N.: thanks all. will paste RFC update link shortly. :thumbsup:
